name: StoneVault instant withdrawal pays uncapped strategy proceeds
summary: StoneVault.instantWithdraw paid the withdrawer whatever StrategyController.forceWithdraw returned, not the burned shares' value, and the Balancer/Aura rETH strategy exited more WETH than asked. The attacker flash-borrowed 8,600 ETH, deposited, called the permissionless rollToNextRound to push it into the strategies, and instant-withdrew more than it put in.
notes: The Balancer/Aura strategy is a target because its exit returned 4,763.09 ETH where the vault asked it for 55% of 8,579.78 ETH; the other strategies returned slightly less than asked. No strategy or ratio change happened between deployment and the exploit.

Loss is the StakeStone strategies' net depletion in the transaction: Aura vault shares (1:1 B-rETH-STABLE BPT, priced as the BPT) and idle ETH. The sfrxETH and stETH the attacker's deposit left in other strategies are not subtracted (rule 11); the attacker itself kept 17.07 ETH gross.
